mri_text: brain mri: 11022023 10:45 am clinical history: 55-year-old with right temporal glioblastoma (grade iv) post gross total resection in september 2023. follow-up evaluation. comparison: mri of the brain dated september 15, 2023. technique: axial and coronal t2 flair, axial diffusion-weighted imaging, axial t1, and coronal postcontrast t1 sequences at 3.0 tesla. additional dynamic gadolinium-enhanced axial perfusion imaging was performed to assess cerebral blood volume. findings: there are findings consistent with prior right temporal craniotomy with a surgical cavity located within the right superior temporal gyrus. postsurgical changes are evident, including alteration in the composition of fluid and blood products within the cavity. there is a slight interval increase in hyperintense t2 flair signal within the right temporal lobe adjacent to the surgical cavity. faint enhancement is noted anterior to the surgical cavity correlating with an area of reduced diffusion observed on the postoperative exam from september 15, 2023. no suspicious nodular enhancement is seen within the brain parenchyma, including at the resection site. linearly oriented decreased signal is visible within the right cerebellum, consistent with prior hemorrhage, decreased in size compared to the previous study. the remainder of the brain parenchyma shows normal signal characteristics. there is mild enlargement of the temporal horn of the right lateral ventricle. the ventricles are otherwise normal in size and position. impression: 1. Compared to the prior mri from september 15, 2023, there is a slight interval increase in hyperintense t2 flair signal within the right temporal lobe adjacent to the surgical cavity, likely representing evolving postsurgical changes. continued monitoring with follow-up imaging is advised. focal enhancement anterior to the surgical cavity correlates with the site of reduced diffusion on the postoperative mri. 2. Evolving right cerebellar hematoma, decreased in size compared to the prior study. end of impression:

assay is designed to identify chromosomal deletions involving the 1p36 and 19q13 regions. it utilizes two vysis(tm) dual-color dna probe sets. probe set one includes the loci-specific identifier (lsi) 1p36 that hybridizes to the 1p target on chromosome 1, producing an orange signal while lsi 1q25 serves as a reference probe for 1q, producing a green signal. likewise, probe set two includes lsi 19q13 that hybridizes to the 19q target on chromosome 19, producing an orange signal, and a 19p reference probe lsi 19p13 that produces a green signal. formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded tissue on two glass slides is de-paraffinized and then treated with pepsin to digest tissue proteins and allow for probes to reach target dna. the dna is then heat denatured and subsequently allowed to hybridize with the two probe sets, one per slide. after hybridization, the slides are washed to remove any of the excess unbound probes and the nuclei are counterstained with dapi (4,6 diamidino-2-phenylidole). enumeration of 1p, 1q, 19p and 19q signals is conducted by microscopic examination of cell nuclei using a fluorescence microscope equipped with appropriate excitation and emission filters. educational note: 1p19q deletion by fish is not an fda approved test. the test was validated by ucsf clinical laboratories to confirm performance characteristics, in compliance with current guidelines for clinical implementation. the laboratory is cap accredited and clia certified to perform high complexity testing. james p. grenertpathologist signed: 9252023 17:45

mri_text: brain mri: 10152023 3:12 pm clinical history: 37-year-old with left parietal astrocytoma (grade iii) status post subtotal resection in august 2023. follow-up evaluation. comparison: mri brain dated august 12, 2023. technique: axial t1, axial diffusion-weighted imaging, sagittal t2 flair, and axial and coronal post-gadolinium t1-weighted sequences at 3 tesla. findings: demonstration of left parietal craniotomy with expected postsurgical changes including small extra-axial fluid collection measuring approximately 4 mm in thickness and pneumocephalus. evidence of subtotal resection of previously seen expansile mass within the left parietal lobe with peri-cavity reduced diffusion in the anterior aspect of the resection cavity expected to transiently enhance on follow-up imaging. additionally, there is a small right cerebellar hematoma without significant mass effect as seen on image 12 series 4. prominent venous plexus throughout the brain most likely related to intraoperative csf drainage. no evidence of hydrocephalus or herniation. minimal enhancement surrounding the resection cavity, likely postsurgical. impression: left parietal craniotomy with subtotal resection of previously seen nonenhancing expansile mass within the left parietal lobe. small right cerebellar hematoma without significant mass effect. prominence of the venous system most notable involving the venous plexus likely related to intraoperative csf drainage. findings discussed with neurosurgery np jennifer lee by neuroradiology dr. mark chen at 1500 on 10152023. end of impression:
